title: Three southern binaries reject a quadratic common timing drift with doubled errors in a 207-system test
abstract: We test whether a common quadratic eclipse ephemeris explains published ASAS-3 and TESS timing measurements. A sampling-aware contrast allows opposite affine primary and secondary trends in each survey. Nine of 207 eligible binaries reject the quadratic model at nominal p < 0.001; eight pass a 0.05 / 207 threshold. Three pass that threshold with fitted errors doubled and after tested single-measurement deletions. They are ASAS 114540-6816.3, 112601-2229.0 and 140808-5906.3. Synthetic cancellation, a seven-parameter coefficient fit and 207,000 fixed-error noise trials check the method. This tests a steady-drift explanation. It does not confirm third stars or periodic signals. Source template errors, correlations, selection and non-affine apsidal effects limit the interpretation. Code, hashes, aggregate results and external-scratch regeneration instructions are preserved.
